Klasse ShutdownHookRegistry

java.lang.Object
org.quurz.foomp.base.misc.ShutdownHookRegistry
public class ShutdownHookRegistry extends Object

A registry for application shutdown hooks with priority-based execution and timeout support.

This class allows registration of shutdown hooks that will be executed when the JVM terminates normally. Hooks are executed in order of priority (higher priority first), and each hook can have an individual timeout. If a hook exceeds its timeout, it will be interrupted and the next hook will be executed.

All hooks are executed sequentially even if some fail. Exceptions are logged but do not prevent other hooks from running. This ensures maximum reliability during shutdown.

Instances are created using the builder pattern via shutdownHookRegistry(). The registry must be explicitly installed using install() to activate it.

Example usage: 

    var registry = ShutdownHookRegistry.shutdownHookRegistry()
        .withLogAdapter(myLogger)
        .register("Database", 100, database::close, Duration.ofSeconds(5))
        .register("Cache", 50, cache::flush, Duration.ofSeconds(3))
        .build();
    registry.install();

  • Methodendetails

    • shutdownHook

      public static ShutdownHookRegistry.ShutdownHook shutdownHook(@NonNull String name, int priority, @NonNull Runnable action, @NonNull Duration timeout)

      Creates a new shutdown hook with the specified parameters.

      Parameter:
      name - the name of the hook for identification in logs; must not be null
      priority - the execution priority; higher values execute first; must be non-negative
      action - the action to execute on shutdown; must not be null
      timeout - the maximum execution time; must be positive
      Gibt zurück:
      a new shutdown hook
      Löst aus:
      NullPointerException - if name, action, or timeout is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if priority is negative or timeout is not positive
      Seit:
      1.0.0
